- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is consistently negative (≤-0.33), model often underestimates; adjust upward, especially if recent price is falling.
- After sharp price spikes, model frequently overshoots in the next 5–10 days; apply a downward correction of 2–5% of spike magnitude.
- If sentiment shifts from positive to negative mid-horizon, model often fails to adjust; reduce forecast slope or add a mean-reversion term.
- For 30-day forecasts, model tends to overreact to short-term sentiment volatility; smooth out extremes using a 7-day moving average filter.
- If sentiment is neutral (0.00–0.33) and price is trending, model often misses the trend; align forecast with recent 14-day average.
- When sentiment is mixed (±0.33), model often averages out; use sentiment-weighted median of recent 5–7 days for correction.
